The test image shows coffee leaves with multiple circular, dark brown spots scattered across the leaf surface. Some whitish/pale patches are also visible on one leaf. The spots are distinct and roughly uniform in size and shape.

Key observations:
- Circular, dark brown lesions on upper leaf surface
- Spots appear on multiple leaves
- Some whitish/pale necrotic patches visible
- No serpentine mines (rules out Miner), no orange powdery pustules (rules out Rust)

Top candidates: **Brown_Eye_Spot** or **Cerscospora** — both cause circular brown lesions on coffee leaves.

Now I'll view one reference image.

The Brown_Eye_Spot reference shows blackened coffee **berries/cherries** — not the leaf spot pattern in the test image. This means the test image's circular brown leaf spots more likely belong to **Cerscospora**, which causes discrete circular brown lesions on coffee leaves.

The test image features:
- Circular, dark brown spots on leaf upper surface (classic Cercospora leaf spot pattern)
- Whitish/pale necrotic centers on some lesions (consistent with aging Cercospora spots)
- Distributed across multiple leaves on the branch

This matches Cercospora coffeicola foliar symptoms. Brown_Eye_Spot in this dataset appears to represent berry-stage symptoms rather than leaf spots.
